items.title: 14.11 Methods and techniques to measure and monitor air quality

blocks.text: Measuring and monitoring air quality combines methods and techniques to assess the concentration of pollutants such as particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, ozone and VOCs; environmental engineers use various methods to measure air quality accurately. The instrument used to measure the Air Quality Index is the nephelometer, which monitors PM such as dust, smoke, mist and fumes; also known as a photometer, it detects particles by measuring the total amount of light they scatter.

blocks.prompt: What does a nephelometer measure, and on what principle?
blocks.explanation: It measures particulate matter, dust, smoke, mist and fumes, by shining light through the air sample and measuring the total light scattered by the particles; more scattering means more particulate matter.

items: Monitoring covers PM, NO2, SO2, CO, O3 and VOCs; the nephelometer (photometer) measures PM by light scattering.
